title: Tenali Raman Tale 150 (தமிழ்)

full_text:
King Krishnadevaraya, feeling restless and weary of courtly flattery, summoned Tenali Raman to his private chamber at midnight:
'Tenali, put on the coarse wool cloak of an ordinary night watchman. We shall walk through the sleeping quarters of Vijayanagara to see how our subjects fare when they believe no Emperor watches them.'

The King and Tenali slipped through a secret postern gate into the quiet city.
They walked through the weavers' quarter, where loom lamps burned late as tired mothers finished fabric for the morning market.
In the bakers' lane, they smelled fresh bread being prepared for the hungry porters.
At the city hospital, they observed selfless physicians tending the sick by candlelight without asking for pay.

In a dark alley near the grain market, they encountered a municipal patrol captain shaking down an elderly vegetable vendor, demanding bribes.
Before the King could draw his sword in wrath, Tenali stepped forward in the shadows, raised his heavy wooden night watchman's staff, and shouted in the voice of the Chief Constable:
'Halt! Inspection by the Royal Guard!'
The corrupt captain dropped his loot, took to his heels, and fled into the night!

The grateful vegetable vendor bowed to the two disguised watchmen, handing them two fresh, sweet mangoes:
'Take these, honest brothers; you have protected my family's bread tonight.'

The King accepted the mango with deep reverence, tears glistening in his eyes.
As dawn broke over the Tungabhadra River, King Krishnadevaraya turned to Tenali on the palace balcony:
'Tenali, tonight I saw the true soul of my empire.
I saw the toil of the weaver, the charity of the physician, the vulnerability of the poor vendor, and the corruption that hides in dark corners.
A ruler who sits only on a golden throne sees only what flatterers want him to see; but he who walks the night with an honest companion sees the living heart of his people.'

The King promoted the selfless physicians, dismissed the corrupt patrol officers, lowered taxes on working weavers, and thanked Tenali Raman for being his eternal compass of truth.
moral: A sovereign who walks among his people learns their real needs, guided by the lantern of honest counsel. [TA]
